title: Best Dehumidifier for Mini Split Homes (2026): Dry Mode & More
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for Mini-Split Homes
dek: Ductless heat pumps cool beautifully and dry the air only some of the time. Here's how to close the humidity gap.
description: The best dehumidifier for mini split homes, plus whether mini splits dehumidify, how dry mode works on Mitsubishi and Daikin units, and when to add one.
intro: Choosing a **dehumidifier for a mini split** home sounds like it shouldn't be necessary. Ductless heat pumps are efficient, quiet and, yes, they do dehumidify while they cool. But plenty of mini-split owners still find their homes sticky in spring and fall, clammy overnight, or damp in the rooms that don't have a head of their own.

The reason is that a mini split's main job is temperature. Its inverter compressor is brilliant at slowing down to hold a setpoint, and at very low speeds the indoor coil can run too warm to condense much water. Dry mode helps, but it doesn't let you dial in a humidity number. A dedicated dehumidifier fills the gap, as long as you choose one that's the right size and quiet enough for living spaces.
Below are the dehumidifiers that pair best with ductless systems, along with a plain-English guide to mini-split dry mode on Mitsubishi, Daikin and other brands.

blocks.text: Yes. Any time a mini split is cooling, warm room air crosses the indoor coil, water condenses on it and drains out through the condensate line. On hot, humid afternoons, a properly sized system removes plenty of moisture.

The trouble comes when the cooling load is small. An inverter compressor slows down to match the load, and at low speeds the coil runs warmer, sometimes above the dew point, so it removes little or no water. That's why mini-split homes can feel clammy in spring, fall and overnight, even though the temperature is spot-on.

items: **Oversized heads** satisfy the thermostat quickly and spend more time at low speed.
**Rooms without a head** — bathrooms, closets, basements — get little drying.
**Mild, rainy weather** brings humidity without heat, so there's nothing for the system to respond to.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for mini-split homes

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. We compared capacity under the 2019 DOE test, ENERGY STAR listings, Consumer Reports' published noise and humidistat ratings, and manufacturer manuals for drainage and controls. We also read mini-split manufacturers' manuals for how their dry modes behave, and owner reviews for recurring complaints.
Because mini splits usually serve living spaces rather than unfinished basements, we weighted noise, footprint and humidistat precision highly, alongside efficiency for long seasonal run times.

sections.heading: What to look for in a dehumidifier for a mini split home

items.label: A set-percentage humidistat
items.text: Dry mode can't hold a humidity number. Your dehumidifier should. Our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/) has seasonal targets.

items.label: Quiet operation
items.text: Mini splits are whisper-quiet, so a loud dehumidifier stands out. Look for sleep modes and good noise ratings.

items.label: Right-sized capacity
items.text: About 20 pints for a bedroom, 35–50 for an open living area. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) has the details.

items.label: Smart placement
items.text: Keep the dehumidifier away from the head's airflow so the two don't fight over the same air.
sub: Aim the dehumidifier's exhaust into the room, not at the head.
Leave a foot or more of clearance on all sides.

items.label: A humidity reading
items.text: A cheap hygrometer in each zone shows whether dry mode alone is enough.

blocks.text: Nearly every ductless system has a dry mode, usually marked with a water-drop icon. It runs the compressor at a low speed with a slow indoor fan, so the coil gets colder relative to the airflow and condenses more water. It still cools the room somewhat, and it uses your temperature setting as a guide rather than a humidity target.

Select Dry on the remote or app and set a temperature close to what you want the room to be. On many Mitsubishi models the unit controls fan speed automatically in dry mode, and the compressor may cycle off once the room cools to setpoint. It works well on warm, muggy days; on cool damp ones, it can overcool the room before the air feels dry.

Daikin's dry mode works on the same principle: low fan, controlled compressor, some cooling. As with Mitsubishi, most residential models don't let you set a humidity percentage, so check the manual for how your specific unit handles fan speed and setpoint in dry mode.
Is there a mini split with a dehumidifier built in?

Every mini split dehumidifies while cooling, and dry mode is effectively the built-in dehumidifier. What's rare is true humidity control, where you set 50% and the system holds it regardless of temperature. Until you have that, a separate dehumidifier is the reliable way to keep a room in the 40–50% range.

sections.heading: Mini-split dry mode vs. a dedicated dehumidifier

blocks.text: The pattern most owners settle on: let the mini split cool and dry on hot days, run dry mode on warm, sticky ones, and let a dehumidifier hold 45–50% the rest of the time. If you also have a window or portable AC in part of the house, our [air conditioner dehumidifier](/best/best-air-conditioner-dehumidifier/) guide covers how those dry modes compare.

Mini splits do dehumidify, but only while they're working hard to cool. For open living areas, the **Midea Cube 50** is the best dehumidifier for mini-split homes; for bedrooms, the quieter **Midea Cube 20**. Choose the **Aprilaire E080** for whole-home control without ducts for heating and cooling, and the **Frigidaire FFAP5033W1** for a damp lower level with no drain. Start with a hygrometer like the **Govee H5179** to see whether you need one at all.

faqs.a: Yes, whenever they're cooling. Water condenses on the indoor coil and drains away. But when the cooling load is light, the inverter slows down and the coil may run too warm to remove much moisture, so homes can feel clammy on mild, humid days.

faqs.q: Do I need a dehumidifier if I have a mini split?
faqs.a: Not always. Put a hygrometer in the main rooms for a week. If humidity stays below about 55%, your system is handling it. If it regularly climbs above 60%, especially overnight or on cool rainy days, add a dehumidifier.

faqs.q: What does mini-split dry mode do?
faqs.a: It runs the compressor at low speed with a slow fan to favor moisture removal over cooling. It still lowers the temperature somewhat and doesn't hold a specific humidity setting.

faqs.q: How do I use dehumidify mode on a Mitsubishi mini split?
faqs.a: Choose Dry on the remote or app and set a temperature close to your comfort setting. Many Mitsubishi models control the fan automatically in dry mode. If the room gets too cold before it feels dry, switch back to cool and run a separate dehumidifier.

faqs.q: Does a Daikin mini split have a dehumidifier mode?
faqs.a: Yes. Daikin units include a dry mode that works much like other brands': low fan, controlled compressor, some cooling. Check your model's manual for how it handles fan speed and setpoint.

faqs.q: Should I run dry mode or cool mode on my mini split?
faqs.a: Use cool mode on hot days; it dries plenty while it runs. Use dry mode when it's warm and sticky but not hot. On cool, damp days, neither works well, which is when a dehumidifier earns its keep.

faqs.q: Can I run a dehumidifier and a mini split at the same time?
faqs.a: Yes. Keep them apart so they're not pulling in the same air, set the dehumidifier to 45–50%, and leave the mini split in cool or heat. The dehumidifier adds a little warmth, which the mini split handles easily.
